question: Where does the detail a Claude Code-style transcript needs (tool arguments, tool result summary, timestamps, call↔result pairing) come from?

options.label: Core renders a richer LogLine
options.reason: Each host adapter in hosts.ts already parses the host's events; it adds the argument summary, a result line and a timestamp to LogLine. The dashboard and `sober logs` read the same enriched line, so the two surfaces stay one vocabulary (logs/data.ts already insists on that).
options.costLater: Every host adapter changes and each needs its own tests; a host that adds event types means adapter work before the screen shows it. LogLine grows fields both ends must keep in step.

options.label: Dashboard works with today's lines
options.reason: No schema, core or CLI change: tool blocks group adjacent lines, timers use the browser clock from when a line arrived. Fastest to ship.
options.costLater: Claude tool lines stay a bare name — no `Read(path)`, no `⎿ 92 lines`, so the session look is half there. Timers are wrong for a finished run replayed from disk. line-detail becomes empty work.

options.label: Send raw host events to the browser
options.reason: The browser gets everything the host said and the dashboard can render any detail it likes without touching core.
options.costLater: Five host event formats parsed in the browser as well as in core: two renderers that drift, and `sober logs` falls behind the screen. Moves parsing across the ADR 0008 line that says the browser reaches core only through server.

derived: packages/schema/src/wire.ts (LogLine is rendered by core, drawn by the screen) and apps/dashboard/src/logs/data.ts (CLI and screen share one vocabulary)
